entries.owner: Joshua + Claude (post-Batch-2a discipline maintained throughout — every claim about file contents inspected before commit)
entries.rationale: Batch 2d shipped the useRole hook but no consumer existed in the codebase. Batch 2e builds ProtectedRoute as the hook's first concrete consumer — the canonical mechanism for gating routes by role/capability. The smoke-test wrap on `/` proves the integration end-to-end: when a user navigates to the protected route, RoleProvider's Promise.all fires, ProtectedRoute reads the resulting context, and renders one of four states based on the resolution.

design_notes.path_a_chosen_over_path_b: Path A: context-Provider pattern mirroring useBranding/BrandingProvider. Path B: TanStack Query useQuery via @tanstack/react-query (which IS installed at App level but unused for data fetching). Chose Path A for v1 to preserve stack consistency — only one fetching pattern in the codebase. TanStack Query adoption is OI-63, a stack-wide migration decision (useBranding would migrate too).
design_notes.honest_delta_from_stage_b_aspirational: Original Stage B useRole_hook_contract declared aspirational features that did NOT ship: seniorityTier 0..6, capabilities string[], hasCapability(cap), isMD(), isChief(), displayName. The backend example referenced unimplemented modules (utils/rbac_matrix.py with resolve_capabilities, _resolve_seniority_tier in role_taxonomy.py). Hook declared at @/lib/role using useQuery. Batch 2d shipped a smaller hook consuming what role_taxonomy.classify_role() actually returns today (tier, branch_scope, sbu, can_be_tagged) plus what the endpoints actually return (is_admin, can_view_all, accessible_modules). Per CGR1 — doctrine bends to reality, not reality to doctrine. The deferred features each require their own architectural sub-decision and are tracked as OI-59..63.
design_notes.derived_state_pattern: isAdmin, canViewAll, canBeTagged, isAuthenticated computed in the context value object on each render via user?.field ?? false. Not stored as separate useState. Avoids the synchronisation bug class where stored derivations drift out of sync with their source state. Helper predicates (userHasTier, userHasAnyRole) are closures over `user` — re-created each render with the current user value.
design_notes.graceful_failure_design: RoleProvider's .catch handler captures fetch failures (e.g. 401 before login when AuthProvider is still a stub) and surfaces them as error state in context. Loading flips false in .finally regardless of success/failure. Consumers see error+!loading and can render an unauthenticated state without the app crashing. BrandingProvider continues to work independently — branded login pages can render even when role fetch fails.

entries.title: /api/roles/registry endpoint (canonical role registry for React)
entries.owner: Joshua + Claude (code-grounded inspection of role_taxonomy public API and existing router patterns)
entries.rationale: The React useRole() hook needs schema-level role data — every classified role plus enum constants for tiers/SBUs/scopes — to answer 'what are all the SBUs?' or 'is role X canonical?' client-side without re-hitting the API. Batch 2b shipped /api/auth/whoami-detailed (per-user identity); Batch 2c ships the complementary /api/roles/registry (canonical schema). FRONTEND_GOVERNANCE originally declared this as /api/roles/me but the semantic is closer to a registry than a 'me' endpoint — renamed and doctrine updated to match.
changes: utils/api_roles.py: new file (~100 lines). Router with prefix /api/roles and tags [roles]. Single endpoint GET /registry. Auth via Depends(get_current_user) — authenticated but not role-gated. Response shape: {enums: {tiers, sbus, scopes}, roles: [{role, tier, branch_scope, sbu, matched_via, can_be_tagged}, ...], total_classified_roles: int}. Iterates list_all_classified_roles() (49 roles), classifies each via classify_role(), converts RoleClassification dataclass via dataclasses.asdict(), derives can_be_tagged inline. design_notes.auth_posture: Authenticated but not role-restricted. Registry is published system schema, not a secret. Public would expose org structure to anonymous; role-gated would prevent React hook initialisation for non-admin users. Authenticated-but-open is the calibrated middle.
design_notes.explicit_only_in_registry: Response includes only EXPLICITLY classified roles (49 in role_classification config). Keyword-fallback rescues are runtime safety net, not canonical declaration. If a role isn't in registry, React side should treat as needing explicit classification before UI decisions depend on it.
design_notes.no_audit: Registry reads are frequent (every page load on React side calls the hook). Unaudited matches existing /api/auth/me and /api/branding precedent for read-only schema endpoints.
design_notes.rename_decision: Path B chosen over Path A. Path A would rename /api/auth/whoami-detailed to /api/roles/me — same data twice under different URL. Path B (this batch) ships a genuinely new endpoint serving a different query (schema vs identity). Semantic clarity gain justifies additional surface.

entries.title: Credit Admin migrated to PostgreSQL-authoritative storage with row-locked disbursement serialization (money-path concurrency P0 closed)
entries.owner: Joshua + Claude (CGR1 maintained: every fix grounded in same-session code inspection + RED-probe-first)
entries.rationale: Credit Admin held the disbursement money-path on a JSON store with no concurrency control. Probes proved real data-loss/double-spend holes: lost-update on distinct cases, lost-append on one case, and same-case double-disburse (10/10 concurrent troops/disburse all succeeded = 10 GL postings + 10x BSC credit for one loan). Migrated to PG with row-level locking; each hole closed by a fix whose RED->GREEN flip is the proof.
changes: CA-1 (88820eb): lossless PG mirror of credit_admin (scalars + complete-case data JSONB, 2 indexes); reads still JSON.

CA-2 (cbc983d): PG-authoritative reads + transactional SELECT...FOR UPDATE row-locked RMW via install_credit_admin_concurrency(); save()-hook universal write chokepoint (captures route-level troops mutations).
CA-3 (7ca9e35): troops book/value-date/disburse became row-locked CreditAdminManager methods in _MUTATION_METHODS; routes slimmed; K001 autopopulate + audit run winner-only.
entries.verification: stress_credit_admin.py A 10/10, B 10/10, C double-disburse 10/10->1/N; simulate_credit_chain.py 295/295 at each step. Committed probe is the standing gate.
entries.cross_references: RL5 canonical migration registry; OPERATIONAL_PROTOCOL silent-except + Trap #15 stale-process; pairs with auth-store entry.

entries.title: UserManager._load made read-only; cross-cutting enrichment scope race (spurious 403/404 under load) eliminated
entries.owner: Joshua + Claude (mechanism pinned by instrumentation, not hypothesis; prior B3/B4 attempts had failed by guessing)
entries.rationale: _enrich_identity_from_store (auth_jwt.py) constructed a fresh UserManager() per request, and _load() called self._save(users) on EVERY load (admin normalization). Under concurrency the simultaneous os.replace(tmp, users.json) collided on Windows (WinError 5); _load raised, _enrich's 'except Exception: pass' swallowed it, staff_code never filled, cascade scope empty -> spurious 403/404 on the user's OWN resources (~50% under load). The atomic write that fixed CORRUPTION had introduced CONTENTION. Affected every scoped endpoint.
changes: utils/core.py: UserManager._load() is READ-ONLY. Admin normalization in memory; users.json persisted ONLY when admin genuinely absent (first-run seed), best-effort. Common path performs zero writes.
scripts/stress_auth_scope.py: committed RED->GREEN gate (R concurrent scoped reads, U concurrent scoped updates, L fresh-login+read storm).
entries.verification: In-process trace pinned every failure to _load -> _save -> os.replace WinError 5. After fix: Probe R/U/L spurious-403/404 ~50% -> 0/N; trace 100% outcome=OK; simulate 295/295. Commit 5c34117.
entries.cross_references: Supersedes efb8fbd hypothesis (self-heal writes); true cause was _load's unconditional save. OPERATIONAL_PROTOCOL silent-except (existing) + Trap #15 (new).
